### Add boundary contracts (B12): a Spring Boot module's routes, listeners, schedules, bean definitions and configuration keys, the advice on each bean, and the places where an annotation does not do what it says, read from the class files (verification pending)

change `mmvrtoznssuo` · [log `e73c9fd621ca`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/a08d738e-5517-4e20-9807-72e419657081/e73c9fd621ca07e47866ecbfa13bc37a7e498352653357005c0cc27998d585ff.jsonl.gz)

What changed: the class-file reader now parses RuntimeVisibleAnnotations, RuntimeVisibleParameterAnnotations, the Exceptions attribute and generic Signature attributes (lib/src/classfile/annotations.rs, signature.rs). A new contract kind, boundaries.contract (lib/src/boundaries.rs), lists every bean with framework annotations (Spring, Jakarta Validation and Transactions, Resilience4j, Micrometer), one line per entry point with its route composed from the class and method mappings, the handler's signature with its parameter annotations and generic types, @ConfigurationProperties keys in Boot's relaxed form, and the advice on each member as indented lines. It then checks what the framework will do with each annotation and records the places where it does nothing as '!' lines: a @Transactional or @PreAuthorize method called on 'this' from the same bean (the receiver is found by a backwards walk over the bytecode's stack effects, lambdas included), advice on a private, static or final method or a final class, a @Transactional method whose declared checked exception commits because rollbackFor does not name it, an @Async method whose non-Future result is lost, a @Cacheable void method, a @Scheduled method with parameters, and constraints on a method that is neither a request handler nor on a @Validated bean. 'jvmcontract boundaries CLASSES' prints it, 'verify'/'update --add boundaries' check and write it like the capability and API contracts, with a boundaries-changed SARIF rule anchored to the first added member. Why: a Spring Boot service is mostly boundaries, none of which is in the code's control flow, so no unit test shows a dropped guard, a widened route, a changed rollback rule or a proxy that is bypassed; the contract makes them a one-line diff a reviewer approves, and the '!' lines are the Spring bugs experts know by name and still ship. Also: the three Box Office modules with Spring annotations carry their boundary contracts in src/contract, checked by a new boxoffice.boundaries Gradle convention (Exec, skipped when jvmcontract is not on the PATH); approach B12 in examples/approaches.md and the router; a B12 runner in build.py (Gradle compileJava of the patched copy, then jvmcontract verify); a spring-boot domain tag; example 110 (an Idempotency-Key header added to POST /orders loses the body's @Valid, expected violation). How verified: new Spring fixtures under lib/tests/fixtures/spring (stand-in annotation types under the real package names) exercise every entry kind and every problem once, and the integration test checks the rendered contract line by line, the round trip through parse, the update/verify flow and that a dropped @PreAuthorize is reported as a violation anchored to the handler; 69 unit and 29 integration tests pass. Running the tool over the real ticketing-service, payment-service and messaging classes gives 19, 6 and 4 beans with 13, 3 and 9 entry points and no problems, as expected of a codebase with programmatic transactions. Verification pending: job 20261103-025524-example-110-an-idempotency-key-header-on runs example 110 through build.py, which needs Gradle.
